summary: cchsflow ships 17 datasets in data/ (12 PUMF 200-row samples, 3 orphaned synthetic _s sets, plus variables/variable_details worksheets) under LazyData:true, 884KB compressed. The central design problem is that the harmonization worksheets exist as three competing artifacts: canonical inst/extdata/*.csv, data/*.RData lazy data consumed by the legacy rec_with_table engine, and an inst/extdata/*.RData cache that load_worksheet_metadata() auto-writes into the installed package directory at runtime (a CRAN policy violation that also leaked generated binaries into git). There is no data-raw/ directory and never has been; RData rebuilds are manual ('match old column structure when rebuilding'), have drifted historically (16 vs 23 columns), were deleted as 'obsolete' in July 2025 and rebuilt three times since, producing 80 v3 commits of binary churn. Sample provenance is documented (StatCan licence, OSF DDI links) but not reproducible (no script, no seed); newest harmonized cycles (cchs2019_2020_p, cchs2022_p, cchs2023_p) have no sample data so cannot be tested in-package; and packaging hygiene (3MB logo PDF in man/figures, unignored ceps/ etc., duplicated CSV+RData worksheets) explains most of the 7.3MB installed size. v4 should collapse to one canonical worksheet artifact with a scripted data-raw/ rebuild and consider a companion data package for samples.

issues.title: Package writes RData into its own installation directory at runtime
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/worksheet-loaders.R:59-62 — 'Auto-save to RData for future performance' calls save_metadata_to_rdata(metadata, metadata_type, rdata_file)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/worksheet-loaders.R:35 — rdata_file <- system.file('extdata', paste0(metadata_type, '.RData'), package = 'cchsflow') i.e. the installed library path
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/worksheet-loaders.R:114-125 — save_metadata_to_rdata() writes via save() with only a tryCatch warning on failure
git show 9dc39582 — 'inst/extdata/variables.RData Bin 0 -> 20209 bytes': the auto-saved cache was accidentally committed to git in the past
.gitignore does not exclude inst/extdata/*.RData (only the bare '.RData' workspace file)
issues.why_design_issue: CRAN policy forbids packages writing anywhere but tempdir()/R_user_dir(). On read-only site libraries every load emits a warning; on writable libraries it silently mutates the installed package, creating a third copy of the worksheets whose content depends on whichever CSV was first read. In dev checkouts the relative fallback path (line 39) writes inst/extdata/*.RData into the repo, which has already been committed by mistake once.
issues.candidate_fix: Delete the auto-save feature. Cache parsed worksheets in a package-level environment (memoise once per session) instead of on disk; if a disk cache is ever needed, use tools::R_user_dir('cchsflow', 'cache'). Add inst/extdata/*.RData to .gitignore as a guard.

issues.title: Three sources of truth for worksheets, two engines reading different copies, no rebuild pipeline
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:170-178 — rec_with_table() defaults to data(variable_details, package='cchsflow') i.e. data/variable_details.RData lazy data
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/worksheet-getters.R:48,63 — get_variables()/get_variable_details() (used by the 3-step engine) read inst/extdata CSVs via load_worksheet_metadata()
git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'data-raw/*' returns nothing: a data-raw/ directory has never existed; exec/check-worksheets.R and exec/fix-worksheets.R contain no save()/RData rebuild code

Project memory: 'RData rebuild after worksheet changes ... The RData files have fewer columns than the CSVs (16 vs 23 for variable_details, 10 vs 18 for variables). Match old column structure when rebuilding' — documented historical schema drift between CSV and RData
Current state verified in sync only after an uncommitted-then-committed repair: variables 418x18 and variable_details 3839x23 identical between CSV and RData (Rscript comparison, 2026-06-11)
tests/testthat/test-data.R:1-43 only asserts data.frame class, non-null columns, nrow>0 — would not catch CSV/RData divergence
issues.why_design_issue: The same metadata lives in inst/extdata/*.csv (canonical, hand-edited), data/*.RData (consumed by rec_with_table), and the runtime extdata RData cache (consumed by the 3-step engine when use_rdata=TRUE). Rebuilds are manual and undocumented (CONTRIBUTING.md has no rebuild instructions), so the two recoding engines can silently operate on different metadata — which already happened (column-count drift). This is the data-layer twin of the dual-engine problem v4 must resolve.
issues.candidate_fix: Pick one canonical artifact (the CSVs). Add data-raw/build-worksheet-data.R that regenerates data/*.RData from the CSVs deterministically (fixed compression, version), wire it into CI with a check that fails when RData != CSV, and make both engines load through a single accessor. Longer term (v4): drop the RData worksheets entirely and parse CSV once into a session cache.

issues.title: Stale-cache preference and inconsistent use_rdata defaults can silently serve outdated metadata
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/worksheet-loaders.R:43-53 — if use_rdata && file.exists(rdata_file), the RData is returned with no mtime/hash comparison against the CSV
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/worksheet-loaders.R:32 — load_worksheet_metadata(..., use_rdata = TRUE) default
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/worksheet-getters.R:48 and :222-224 — get_variables() and get_variable_details() default use_rdata = FALSE, the opposite default
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/worksheet-loaders.R:39-40 — dev fallback paths file.path('inst','extdata',...) are relative to getwd(), so behaviour depends on the caller's working directory
issues.why_design_issue: After a worksheet CSV edit, any previously auto-saved RData wins silently — exactly the failure mode for a metadata-driven package where the worksheets ARE the product. The opposite defaults across the public API mean callers get different freshness guarantees (and different performance: use_rdata=FALSE re-reads the ~1MB CSV on every get_variables() call) depending on entry point, and the cwd-relative fallback makes dev results location-dependent.
issues.candidate_fix: Remove the use_rdata branch entirely; read the CSV once per session into a package environment with an explicit refresh function. If kept, compare file.mtime(csv) > file.mtime(rdata) before preferring the cache and unify the default across all entry points.

issues.title: Generated binary worksheets tracked in git: 80 v3 commits of churn including delete-as-obsolete-then-rebuild
evidence: git log --oneline v3 -- data/variables.RData data/variable_details.RData | wc -l = 80 commits

git show fad4dcad (2025-07-11) and ae098b22: 'Removes obsolete binary data files ... no longer needed as part of the application's data management strategy' — deleted data/variable_details.RData and data/variables.RData

Subsequent rebuild commits: d50d7aa2 '...rebuilt RData from csv worksheets', f934ebf2 'rebuilt .RData files from updated csv worksheets...', e3fbf85f 'Cleaned csv worksheets ... and rebuild RData as a result'
git rev-list --objects --all -- data/ : 222 blobs, 13.1MB packed for data/ alone
issues.why_design_issue: data/*.RData for the worksheets are pure derivatives of the CSVs, yet every worksheet edit stores a new binary blob that cannot be code-reviewed (PR reviewers cannot diff RData). The July 2025 deletion shows the team itself believed they were obsolete — then the legacy engine's dependence on data() forced them back, the clearest single demonstration that the dual-artifact design is unstable.
issues.candidate_fix: Stop committing derived RData on every change: either generate data/*.RData only at release/build time via data-raw/ + a GHA step, or accept tracking but regenerate exclusively through the scripted pipeline with a CI equality check so churn is intentional and verified.

issues.title: 200-row sample provenance is documented but not reproducible (no script, no seed, ad hoc save settings)
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/README.md:125-128 — 'cchsflow includes a random sample of 200 respondents from each CCHS PUMF file from 2001 to 2018' — no script or seed anywhere in repo or history (git grep across last 200 commits for cchs2001_p creation code: no hits)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/data.R:38-67 — good licence/source documentation (StatCan Open Licence, OSF DDI links, 'accessed Jan 2020') but no extraction method
tools::checkRdaFiles('data'): cchs2001_p.RData compress=xz while all other samples are gzip; samples are serialization version 2, worksheets version 3 — fingerprints of one-off manual saves
File mtimes: _p samples frozen 2022-02-22 / 2022-09-08; _s files 2025-06-04 — three different creation events, none scripted
issues.why_design_issue: For a package whose pitch is methodological reproducibility of CCHS harmonization, its own bundled data cannot be regenerated. When new PUMF cycles are added (a v4 goal), there is no recipe to produce consistent samples, and nobody can verify that the shipped 200 rows are unmodified PUMF rows versus edited ones.
issues.candidate_fix: Add data-raw/make-cchs-samples.R: read each OSF-hosted PUMF copy, set.seed(<documented>), dplyr::slice_sample(n = 200), save with uniform compress='xz', version=3. Reference the script from R/data.R @source and README.

issues.title: Newly harmonized cycles (2019-2023) have no sample data, so their worksheet rows are untestable in-package
evidence: variables.csv databaseStart references 34 database tokens including cchs2019_2020_p, cchs2022_p, cchs2023_p (Python scan of inst/extdata/variables.csv, 2026-06-11)
data/ contains samples only for 2001-2017_2018 PUMF cycles (12 _p files) plus 3 _s files — no cchs2019_2020_p/cchs2022_p/cchs2023_p RData
Recent v3 commits extend harmonization to these cycles (7407e07a 'Extended alcohol, chronic condition ... variables to 2019-2020', f91c15f4 '2015-2020 Master harmonization')
tests/testthat/test-recode-with-table.R and vignettes rely on the bundled samples as their only data source
issues.why_design_issue: The package's QA model is 'run rec_with_table against the bundled samples'. Every worksheet row targeting 2019-2020/2022/2023 PUMF ships with zero executable verification — regressions in exactly the newest, most active harmonization work are invisible to the test suite. (Master _m cycles are unavoidably untestable, which strengthens the case for explicitly stating the testability boundary.)
issues.candidate_fix: Generate 200-row samples for cchs2019_2020_p, cchs2022_p, cchs2023_p via the same scripted data-raw pipeline (StatCan Open Licence permits redistribution) and add smoke tests that rec_with_table/3-step functions run for every PUMF database token in variables.csv.

issues.title: Orphaned _s datasets ship with self-contradictory documentation
evidence: Python scan: 0 rows of variables.csv reference cchs2009_s/cchs2010_s/cchs2012_s in databaseStart; only R/data.R and tests/testthat/test-data.R mention them
data/cchs2009_s.RData (200x1845), cchs2010_s.RData (200x1955), cchs2012_s.RData (200x1815) — ~200KB shipped

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/data.R:431-446 — titled '2009 CCHS synthetic subset data' / 'Long name: synthetic-CCHS-E-2009-FullSampleFile_F1' yet body says 'Source from Statistics Canada, Canadian Community Health Survey PUMF, accessed May 2022'

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/data.R:437-439 — circular note: 'this subset of respondents may also be in the 2009 synthetic subset' (it IS the 2009 synthetic subset; should reference the overlapping PUMF)
Project memory: '_s databases ... are deprecated share files' mapping to _m equivalents in v3 worksheets
issues.why_design_issue: Datasets that no worksheet row can recode are dead weight users can load but never use with the package's own engine, and the synthetic-vs-PUMF documentation contradiction undermines confidence in data provenance claims (it matters legally whether the rows are PUMF microdata or StatCan synthetic files).
issues.candidate_fix: In v4, either remove the _s datasets (with a NEWS deprecation note) or re-document them accurately as StatCan synthetic full-sample files used to emulate share-file workflows, fix the copy-pasted NOTE text, and decide whether the duplicate_datasets vignette still needs them.

issues.title: Packaging hygiene inflates installed size: 3MB logo PDF, unignored dev directories, worksheets shipped twice
evidence: man/figures/cchsflow-logo.pdf is 3.0MiB (largest file shipped in the package; PNG 67K and SVG 23K versions exist alongside) — man/ totals 4.3MB

.Rbuildignore lacks entries for ceps/ (1.5MB), development/, exec/, extra/, harmonization-development/, CLAUDE.local.md, and R/docs + R/legacy (80K of non-loaded .R files inside R/, which also triggers R CMD check non-standard-files NOTEs)
inst/extdata/variable_details.csv (1.0MiB) + variables.csv (252KB) ship alongside the identical data as data/*.RData lazy data — the worksheet content is installed twice; inst/extdata totals 2.0MB
du: data 916K, inst 2.0M, man 4.3M, R 648K, tests 468K → ~9-10MB tarball content, consistent with the reported 7.3MB installed size vs CRAN's 5MB NOTE threshold
DESCRIPTION has LazyData: true with no LazyDataCompression field
issues.why_design_issue: Most of the installed footprint is avoidable: a vector logo accidentally saved as a 3MB PDF, development artifacts that should never reach the tarball, and the same worksheet data shipped in two formats because two engines read different copies. A 5MB+ installed size draws a CRAN NOTE and makes the 'add more cycles' v4 goal progressively worse.
issues.candidate_fix: Replace/delete the logo PDF (keep SVG/PNG); add ceps, development, exec, extra, harmonization-development, CLAUDE.local.md, R/docs, R/legacy to .Rbuildignore (or relocate R/legacy out of R/); once a single worksheet artifact is chosen (issue 2), stop shipping the other format; set LazyDataCompression: xz when resaving.

issues.title: Sample data growth strategy: bundled samples vs companion data package undecided before v4 cycle expansion
evidence: data/ currently 884KB compressed for 15 sample datasets (12 _p + 3 _s); each new PUMF cycle adds ~40-70KB compressed (200 rows x 1000-1900 columns)
Pending cycles per worksheets/memory: 2019-2020, 2021-2022, 2022, 2023 PUMFs — adding them in-package grows data/ ~25-30% immediately and every two years thereafter

200-row samples already cause sparse-category brittleness: project memory records FVC ~57% valid in 2005 and ~1% valid in 2017-2018 (optional survey content), i.e. some harmonized variables have near-zero non-missing rows to test against
README.md:125-128 positions the samples as vignette/demo data, but tests/testthat/test-recode-with-table.R uses them as the de facto regression fixture
issues.why_design_issue: The bundled-sample model conflates three jobs (vignette demos, regression fixtures, user smoke-testing) in one 200-row artifact that is both too small for sparse variables and a permanent size tax. CRAN convention for growing survey data is a separate data package or download-on-demand; deciding this before v4 avoids re-cutting samples twice.
issues.candidate_fix: Scope decision for cep-017: keep a minimal in-package toy fixture (1-2 cycles) for examples, move the full per-cycle sample collection to a cchsflow.data companion package or OSF download with R_user_dir caching, and size test fixtures per-variable (oversample sparse categories) rather than uniform n=200.

issues.title: Invalid database identifiers in shipped worksheets (cchs2007_2008p / cchs2007_2008m, missing underscore)
evidence: inst/extdata/variables.csv line 84 — variable DEN_132 databaseStart contains 'cchs2007_2008p' (no underscore before p) among otherwise valid tokens
inst/extdata/variable_details.csv lines 534-543 — 10 DEN_132 rows carry the same malformed token; 'cchs2007_2008m' also appears in the worksheet token scan
These tokens match no data/*.RData dataset and no valid database name, so database_name == token can never be satisfied in rec_with_table()
Same failure family as the known 'chs2011_2012_m' missing-c typos recorded in project memory
issues.why_design_issue: Database identifiers are free-text in the CSVs with no closed vocabulary validation, so a one-character typo silently removes a cycle from a variable's coverage (DEN_132 loses 2007-2008) — users get NA with no error. The check-worksheets tooling validates formatting but evidently not identifier validity.
issues.candidate_fix: Fix the DEN_132 tokens; add a worksheet check (exec/check-worksheets.R or schema) validating every databaseStart token against the canonical database list (already enumerable from inst/metadata schemas or a constant), failing CI on unknown identifiers.

issues.title: Repository binary-history bloat: 841MB local .git, full-cycle PUMF file and large PDFs in history
evidence: git count-objects -vH: size-pack 827.93 MiB across 4 packs, two of which are identical 267MiB packs (duplicate packing; prune-packable: 36) — reachable blobs from --all total only ~78MB

Largest historical blobs: data/cchs2003.Rdata 4.7MB packed (a full-cycle CCHS data file once committed, later removed), 10 'inst/extdata/CCHS documentation/*.pdf' files at 2.1-3.1MB each (since removed), extra/smoking-analyses-additional-files/*.pptx 1.1-1.9MB (commit 9c777d1b)
Pack attribution by path: inst 35.4MB, data 13.3MB, man 8.9MB, extra 7.9MB of packed history
Root .DS_Store is git-tracked (git ls-files | grep DS_Store) despite *.DS_Store in .gitignore
issues.why_design_issue: Binary artifacts (data snapshots, meeting PPTXs, scanned PDFs) committed to the package repo permanently tax every clone and CI run; the local 841MB is mostly fixable with gc, but the ~78MB reachable history is not without a rewrite. Since the team already prefers history rewrite over revert commits (project memory), v4 is the natural moment to decide.
issues.candidate_fix: Run git gc/repack locally to collapse duplicate packs. For v4, decide whether to filter-repo the large removed binaries (cchs2003.Rdata, CCHS documentation PDFs, extra/*.pptx) and adopt a policy that meeting artifacts and source PDFs live in OSF/Drive, not the package repo; untrack .DS_Store.
